1.1: 1.1 Tobias. BEDE, in Tobias, tome 2. The book of Tobias is wholesome on the surface of the letter. For it abounds in the greatest examples of moral life, and admonitions. But as fruits excel leaves, so the allegory excels the history. For it contains the greatest sacraments of the Church. For Tobias himself signifies the people of Israel, who with the other nations given to idolatry, served God with right faith and works. Whence: When they went, etc. For Jeroboam who made golden calves to deceive subjects expresses the worshipers of idolatry, whose accomplices are signified in the subjects. Of Nephthali. THE SAME, ibid. Breadth, of which: Your commandment is exceeding broad, Psalm 118., whose tribe, that is the son, the faithful people, his city the Church, of which: A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid, Matthew 15. Above Naasson. Naasson augury, his city augurs the higher things, that is, contemplates the heavenly. BEDE as above. The captivity of Tobias designates the captivity of the human race by the king of all the wicked, that is the devil, who cast us down from the heavenly country into the valley of this exile.
1.3: 1.3 So that all, etc. THE SAME, ibid. So the people of Israel through the teachers of the divine word dispensed alms not only to the unlearned hearers of their own nation, but to the Gentiles coming to Judaism. For whatever of good he naturally had which the captive enemy did not take away, he showed as an example of virtue to his own, and offered a portion of saving knowledge as a tithe of his substance to strangers, that is to the Gentiles.
1.4: 1.4 Yet nothing childish. Now he bore that apostolic saying in his breast: Be not children, etc., 1 Corinthians 14. This, however, is said in respect to those who walked in the commandments of the Lord without blame, according to that rule of Tyconius, by which as speaking of the same, sometimes for the good we praise all, sometimes for the wicked we blame all, which is the second rule.
1.6: 1.6 All the first-fruits. THE SAME, ibid. He seems to speak against this, that the first tithe went to the use of the Levites, the second to be spent on necessaries when the temple was visited. But the tithes of the third year which they were then wont to make they conceded to the poor. And therefore we say all that or all the second, because he could not go to the temple for fear of the king's guards.
1.9: 1.9 But when he was become a man. THE SAME, ibid. So the people of Israel, etc., down to whence: My firstborn Israel, Exodus 4.
1.10: 1.10 Whom from infancy to fear, etc., by believing and confessing, namely, that he would never commit sin, but fill himself with the spirit of the fear of the Lord.
1.13: 1.13 In the sight of Shalmaneser, etc. He does not contradict what is said elsewhere of Shalmaneser, who is also Sennacherib: for he had two names, or generally all the kings of the Medes were so called as the Pharaohs of Egypt.
1.16: 1.16 And when he was come, etc. THE SAME, ibid. So the people of God, etc., down to and lay open the secrets of Scripture.
1.20: 1.20 He gave burial, etc., of sinners: so that not even memory should remain in them. By such burial our fathers wished to be honored next to the burial of Christ. Whence Jacob wished to be buried in Judea, and Joseph commanded concerning his bones.
1.21: 1.21 Finally when he was returned, etc. Well did Sennacherib flee from Judea: for the devil fears true confession: and does not stand before its face.
2.10: 2.10 It happened, etc. BEDE, in Tobias, tome 2. Let no one wonder if sometimes good signifies evil typically, evil good. For if this were not allowed, the name of God would never be written in black ink, but always in shining gold: because God is light. But if you write the name of the devil with a white pebble, it nevertheless signifies darkness. Tobias blinded therefore signifies the people of Israel. For blindness in part has happened in Israel, Romans 2. Wearied with burying he was blinded. For he who perseveres untiring in good works does not admit the light of faith. So spiritually wearied sleeps he who neglects to watch, to stand, to act manfully, and to be strengthened. To whom it is said: Arise, you that sleep, and rise from the dead, Ephesians 5. BEDE, ibid. Swallows, for their light flight, signify pride and levity: whose filth blinds those it falls on. Under a swallow's nest sleeps he who incautiously subjects himself to levity, wantonness and pride. This blindness especially prevailed in the people of Israel, the coming of the Lord in the flesh at hand, when they labored under the yoke of Roman servitude and violated the commandments of the divine law by living ill.
2.14: 2.14 But immovable, etc. Because judgment begins at the house of God. Whence: Begin at my sanctuary, Ezekiel 9. He who is not corrected is not a son: He who spares the rod hates his son, Proverbs 13. Paul as a boy is buffeted, as a young man is exalted.
2.15: 2.15 The kings mocked, etc. BEDE, ibid. There were among the people, etc., down to whence: Charity is patient, is kind, 2 Corinthians 13.
3.7: 3.7 That Sara, etc. BEDE, in Tobias, tome 2. It signifies the crowd of notions, etc., down to Daniel prays in the upper room, and Elisha has upper rooms, and Christ celebrates the pasch in an upper room.
4.3: 4.3 Bury my body. By burying bodies we commit to the earth as a sacred deposit what we believe is to be rendered back and glorified in the resurrection.
5.7: 5.7 Of the children of Israel. For he was of the number of angels, who are children of Israel, because they always see God face to face, and are often sent for the custody of the children of Israel, that is of those seeing God. Whence: I set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel, Deuteronomy 52.
5.10: 5.10 Then entering, etc. BEDE, as above. The angel appeared to Tobias and offered himself as a companion, and the Son of God assumed man, and conversing visibly with men saved the human race. Tobias brought the angel to his father, etc., and the Lord by the miracles which he did in the flesh showed himself to the people of the Jews, from when he had taken flesh: because he is son and angel, that is messenger of the Father's will, to whom he also preached the joy of perpetual salvation, saying: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Matthew 3. And to those despairing of heavenly light: I am, he says, the light of the world, he that follows me walks not in darkness, John 8.
5.15: 5.15 And the angel said to him. THE SAME, ibid. The angel promises Tobias to lead his son into the city of the Medes and bring him back, etc., down to Tobias asking the angel whence he was.
5.18: 5.18 I am, he says, Azarias the son of great Ananias, THE SAME, ibid. Azarias helper, Ananias glory of God. Christ also shows to his faithful that he is he of whom it is said: You are my helper and my deliverer, O Lord, make no delay, Psalm 69. And we saw his glory, as it were of the only begotten of the Father, John 1.
5.22: 5.22 Then all being prepared. BEDE, as above. The Lord appearing in the flesh, etc., down to and so to the salvation of the Gentiles through the apostles it came.
6.1: 6.1 He set out, etc. BEDE, in Esdras, tome 2. The Lord coming to save the Gentiles, etc., down to and defend spiritual sheep from thieves and bestial spirits and heretics.
6.2: 6.2 And behold a fish, etc. BEDE, as above. The sacrament of the Lord's passion is plainly signified, etc., down to nor had the prince of the world coming anything in him. He went out. THE SAME, ibid. Christ accepted death to which he owed nothing, that he might wash his feet, that is his members, from the contagion of sin and death. The fish ran to devour him, and the Lord suffering on the cross the devil came, by whose moving he was crucified, seeking whether he might find any sin in him.
6.3: 6.3 Fearing which, etc. Christ, the moment of death imminent, began to fear and be weary, not the devil, but death, which by the envy of the devil entered the world, shuddering at it by the natural frailty of the flesh; whence: Father, remove this chalice from me, Mark 14.
6.4: 6.4 Take hold of the gill, etc. BEDE, ibid. Christ took hold of the devil who wished to seize him on the cross, and by dying overcame. He took hold therefore of the gill, that the most wicked head he might separate from the body by the right hand of his power, that is take away the wickedness of the ancient enemy from those whom he had made body for himself, and bring them into his body, that is the Church. For the fish has the gill at the boundary of head and body, and Christ is the head of the Church, which is his body, and the devil the head of the wicked, who are his body. When he had done this. Because when the Lord manifested the wickedness of the devil, he yet endeavored to stir up persecution against his elect: for these are his feet by which he walks on earth who reigns over all in heaven.
6.5: 6.5 Open the fish. The Lord opened the fish, when he laid open the wickedness of the devil more widely to the saints: and as it were unlocked the secrets of his snares. He put by for himself the heart of it, because he pointed out his cunning in the Scriptures, of which it is said: The serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth, Genesis 3., and elsewhere: We are not ignorant of his devices, 2 Corinthians 2. He put by the gall also, because with how great fury of malice he rages against the human race, he willed to be written and preserved for zeal of caution. He put by the liver, because he made known his malignant counsels against us through the teachers of truth: For the physicians say: that by the heat and hidden power of the liver food is cooked and digested. When indeed what we plan to do we inquire with careful thought in what order it should be done, we cook as it were with the heat of the liver food received in the stomach. For these are necessary. The cunning and wickedness of the devil known to us profit for medicine: for the more surely we explore them, the more surely we avoid.
6.6: 6.6 He roasted its flesh, etc. BEDE, as above. Whatever of this fish he took for himself, etc., down to until in the Gentiles the foundations of the Church were laid.
6.12: 6.12 And it is fitting. THE SAME, ibid. Raguel signifies the people of the Gentiles, etc., down to and who is worthy to hear: Now I will not call you servants, but my friends, John 15.
7.11: 7.11 Which word heard Raguel was afraid, etc. BEDE, as above. The people of the Gentiles hearing the word of faith, etc., down to that those who said foolish things, might foolishly perish.
8.1: 8.1 And after they had supped, etc. BEDE, in Tobias, tome 2. Tobias, brought to the chamber, took forth, etc. God, about to receive the Church from the Gentiles, at the beginning of betrothal, commands her to renounce the devil, and all his pomps and confess the faith of the holy Trinity for the remission of sins: which is to burn the inner parts of the fish on live coals. BEDE, as above. Because after the renunciation of the devil, after the confession of true faith, follows the remission of sins, by the water of baptism, the devil expelled, he bound the devil: because he restrained him from hurting the faithful, whom, though he is sometimes permitted to tempt for proof, he is yet forbidden to overcome.
8.3: 8.3 He bound him. The desert and Egypt signify the hearts of unbelievers, which are deserted by God, because unworthy of his dwelling, and according to the interpretation of Egypt, obscured by the darkness of their perfidy. Deservedly too, he who is deserted by God is filled by the demon. The angel, however, bound in the desert the demon who wished to kill Tobias, who, restrained from the faithful, who are the members of Christ, permits the devil to rule only in unbelievers, in whom yet he holds him bound, because he is not permitted to hurt even them as much as he strives.
8.11: 8.11 And it came to pass, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The song of the cocks, etc., down to they truly knew Christ, the enemy overcome, to be the bridegroom of the holy Church.
8.17: 8.17 We bless you, O Lord God. THE SAME, ibid. Raguel rejoices over the life of Tobias, etc., down to are fat, filled with the grace of heavenly love.
8.22: 8.22 Also two, etc. THE SAME, ibid. The Apostle of the Gentiles those who had come to the faith, etc., down to who receive banquets from those by whose examples they are refreshed. Four rams. Because the holy teachers and martyrs preserve the four books of the Gospel in faith and work, are fortified with prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance, and instruct the Church of God in the four parts of the world. He caused to be slain. Because some of their own accord mortify their bodies, that they may be a living sacrifice: others among the hands of the unbelieving undergo martyrdoms: by the arms of justice on the right and on the left, that is, in prosperity and adversity, conquering the ancient enemy.
8.23: 8.23 And Raguel adjured Tobias. BEDE, ibid. We adjure Christ that he stay with us, until we obtain the perfection of rest through the grace of the Holy Spirit, by which we may rest both from sins in the body and from wicked thoughts in the mind.
9.3: 9.3 Yet I beseech you. BEDE, from Isidore. Some of the believers serving you to whom you may commit the office of preaching for the gathering of the Gentiles, who have not yet received the mystery of faith, but yet have heard the fame: and the talent of the word which they learned by fame, let them render by obedience of faith. A new people is gathered daily in the Church, yet it can be understood specially of those who received the letter of the law, the seventy interpreters, and therefore received the faith the sooner.
10.8: 10.8 But Raguel, etc. BEDE, as above. When the fullness of the Gentiles shall have entered, no one can prevent the Lord from granting the salvation of Israel, and looking on its blindness, which has happened in part. For the divine clemency remembered that there is great sadness and continual sorrow for the believing Jews because of their unbelieving brethren.
10.10: 10.10 He delivered, etc. The teachers of the Church are sent back at the end to Christ, with the Church herself, full of the riches of virtues, to enlighten the faith, and enrich with the substance of good works the nation of the Jews, from which the Son of God took flesh.
11.3: 11.3 Let us go before. BEDE, as above. After the people of the Gentiles was enlightened, divine grace goes before to illuminate the blindness of the Jews, that in their books they may know Christ true man and true God, and so at last as if the angel and their son seen whom they had long not seen, they may greatly rejoice; at last, namely, may join itself to the Church of the Gentiles, gathered in communion of mysteries.
11.9: 11.9 With fawning. BEDE, as above. The dog rejoiced while he revisited the roofs of his masters long unseen. The teachers rejoice over the effect of their work, when they understand Judea is to be regathered by the Lord. They rejoice over the reward of eternal life, and foretell that with the same reward the hearts of all are to be gladdened, and bring forth that the grace of the Holy Spirit will come at once.
11.10: 11.10 Rising up. The word of salvation heard from the teachers, the people of the Jews rises from the long blindness of their perfidy, and runs with love to the Lord; but stumbling in steps of works, until reborn, instructed in Christ, he perceive the light of faith and working.
11.13: 11.13 Then taking. BEDE, ibid. The Lord plainly reveals to believers how great is the malice of the ancient enemy, who longed to devour him in the passion; but by this slain, he lost his members, that is those whom he held before.
11.14: 11.14 The film. BEDE, ibid. The people of the Jews still has a veil before the face of the heart, etc., down to but those who, conscious of frailty and ignorance, say, Lord God, enlighten my darkness; are enlightened by the Lord.
11.18: 11.18 She entered, etc. THE SAME, ibid. It signifies the light of spiritual grace, which is sevenfold. After seven days of illumination the wife enters: because after Judea has been enlightened by faith, after she has received the grace of the Holy Spirit; the Church will enter to her, that there may be one fold and one shepherd, and the house of Christ be one, firmed by one cornerstone.
12.14: 12.14 And now, etc. BEDE, in Tobias. The angel about to return to heaven explains more openly what he is and why he came, and whither he is to return: and Christ to the same people advancing more widely disclosed his condition, showing that he is in the Father, and the Father in the Son. The angel returns to God, Tobias remains with the Father, and Christ is understood by his faithful as equal to the Father in divinity, consubstantial with men in humanity.
13.1: 13.1 And Tobias opening his mouth. BEDE, in Tobias. He confessed truth and mercy, etc., down to by preaching the joys of the heavenly country.
14.1: 14.1 And after Tobias was enlightened, etc., the number forty is laborious, of fasting and abstinence. We, however, ought to bear all the labors of this life, with love of God and neighbor, and so we shall bear fruit.
14.3: 14.3 For at fifty-six years of age he lost the sight of his eyes, etc. He had passed the sacred number fifty, nor had he reached sixty, which on account of six, in which all things were made, signifies perfection.
14.5: 14.5 And at the hour of his death he called to him Tobias. BEDE, in Esdras. Tobias, that is the teachers of the Jews, who about to depart from this world announce to their kinsmen: that the world draws near to its end, and the goods of the future life are soon to be.
14.14: 14.14 Tobias departed from Nineveh with his wife, and children, and children's children, etc. THE SAME, ibid. This Christ does daily, etc., down to living long does not leave lightness of mind.
14.16: 14.16 They buried. The burial of Tobias designates the end of the world, in which our Lord with his body, which is the Church, enters into rest, the angels rejoicing together at the society of men, and placing each through the various mansions according to the quality of merits.
